model: Newtonian central gravity, RK4; impulsive spring separation and prograde rocket burn
assumptions: Stationary, nonrotating central point mass; no relativistic trajectory integration or frame dragging.
80 Rs periapsis is chosen to stay away from the strong-field visual environment; Newtonian predictions remain approximate.
Separation conserves linear momentum. Both bodies start at the same point in the point-mass trajectory model.
450 s specific impulse; 4000 kg of retained propellant burned impulsively after stage release.
Passive flyby preserves asymptotic speed in this stationary black-hole frame; the explicit burn changes orbital energy.
Thermal survival, tides, finite burn duration, spin control, disk interactions, and collisions are not simulated.
